sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 978.7 ± 293.3 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Radioligand binding studies performed with HA-RXFP3 (L1); surface expression confirmed by anti-HA western blot for 3xHA-RXFP3 (L5); surface expression confirmed by anti-FLAG IHC for FLAG-RXFP3 (L7, L8). Binding-competent receptor confirms trafficking and folding preserved.
sites.rationale: RXFP3 has no signal peptide in the canonical topology (EC1 spans residues 1–81, TM1 begins at residue 82), so residue 1 (M) is the mature extracellular N-terminus and insert_after_residue=0 is the correct prepend junction. The tag sits >81 residues from the TM1 boundary, satisfying the >=3 aa constraint. L1 explicitly states the ATG was replaced to create HA-RXFP3 and the construct was used in binding studies, establishing both surface delivery and ligand-binding function. Four independent ledger lines (L1, L3/L4, L7, L8) using two different tag types (HA, FLAG) all converge on this single extracellular junction, making it the highest-confidence site in the ledger. Full-length human RXFP3 with 1xHA tag at the N-terminus (pcDNA3.1zeo(+)-HA-RXFP3) was constructed by replacing the ATG start codon with the HA-tagged vector backbone; the construct was expressed in mammalian cells and used in radioligand binding and mutagenesis studies. Additional independent support: L3/L4/L5 (3xHA-RXFP3 in HEK293 cells, western blot confirmed), L7 (N-terminal FLAG on WT and mutant RXFP3 for surface expression measurement), L8 (FLAG + cleavable signal sequence in PRESTO-TANGO, surface expression by IHC).

sources.claim: The 1XHA-tagged human RXFP3 vector (pcDNA3.1zeo (+)-HA-RXFP3) was produced by ligating a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) generated RXFP3 construct missing the ATG start codon and with a Eco RV site at the 5′ end and a Xho I site at the 3′ end following the TGA stop site (primers listed in Table 2 ) into the pcDNA3.1zeo (+)-HA construct.

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines converge on the extracellular N-terminus (insert_after_residue=0) as the sole validated surface-tag site. L2 (HA-RXFP3 Δ1–33) describes a truncated construct in which residues 1–33 are deleted and the HA tag is placed at the new N-terminus; this is not a tag insertion into full-length RXFP3 at a distinct residue and does not define a second junction. L6 describes a cryo-EM engineering construct with an N-terminal HA signal peptide + 10×His + BRIL (same position 0 junction) and a C-terminal LgBiT fusion; the C-terminal fusion lands in IC4 (residues 393–469, intracellular) and is recorded in other_positions. No ledger line reports a tolerated tag insertion in any of the extracellular loops (EC2 141–152, EC3 236–264, EC4 352–367), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: LgBiT subunit fused at the C-terminus of RXFP3 in a cryo-EM stabilisation construct; residue 469 (Y) falls within IC4 (393–469), the intracellular C-terminal tail, so this fusion is cytoplasmic and not a surface-tag site.
